title: Each agent role file and the lane start text carry one short-output line, proven by a check
why: Agents may spend tokens on narration that no reader needs; briefs should carry only task facts.
note: R36 (owner 12:49 and 12:52 CST Nov 11, relayed by the retrospective; plan 567ef25). Owner 12:49: "how much should our subagents be allowed to just \"type\""; 12:52: "im assuming the brief kinda needs to have a line in terms of how much to talk ... keep verbiage to a minimum something like that? or it's mechanized? unsure i'm deferring to you". Pick under that deferral: the short-output line goes in each agent role file (agents/*.md) and the lane start text, never in each brief; briefs carry only task facts; a check proves each role file holds the line; reasoning and tool inputs are never cut. Gate: it ships only if the brief audit (session_013NEJKzHzgAkNwHN3wczJ2X) shows narration is a real share of lane output. Owner 12:55 CST (relayed): "i agree keeping the instruction int he role files is best and agree with that." Brief audit 12:56 CST (retrospective, 7 of the 10 newest lanes): output is 27-42% of lane cost, but one sampled lane's visible output was 91% tool inputs and 4% narration; cache read and write are about 73% of cost. The role-file line waits on a larger sample. Owner 13:10 CST (relayed), R36 widened: "how to keep their prose from staying tight (maybe in their claude.md or mechanically idk or a judge that scans and says hey you yappin too much)". The reply judge gains a flag-only item for a reply longer than its reader needs, judged by reader, never by count. Plan f640fc655: R36 measured, the terse line ships. Prose wave (owner 20:24 CST Nov 11, item 521): the line itself is prose, first wave; the check that proves each file holds it is the code half (retrospective 20:43 CST).
